findings.reason: citing that helper turns the followup into a one-line reuse of a tested resolver and stops the repair from re-deriving path resolution.
findings.text: the followup "Store minted_from repo-relative and repair the twelve dangling values" instructs minting `minted_from` repo-relative but names no existing helper, while `_ledger_relative_path` (imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:205) already returns `root, ledger.relative_to(root).as_posix()` for exactly this purpose in the same module it modifies

findings.reason: naming the owner keeps §3 from adding a fourth-plus duplicate of a mechanism it is chartered to consolidate.
findings.text: "resolve a path to its git root and relativise it" is already implemented four times, each re-running `rev-parse --show-toplevel` against a different cwd: `_ledger_relative_path` (imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:208), `loaded_grammar_checkout` (imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:106), `reviewing_guide_url` (imas_codex/standard_names/release_notes.py:410) and `LabelCache.commit_labels` (imas_codex/clusters/label_cache.py:406); the `minted_from` repair should name and extend one owner (catalog_release.py:205 is the most complete — it returns root plus the posix-relative path and raises on a non-git tree) rather than mint through the site that produced the twelve dangling values and add a fifth resolution point under §3, the one section whose stated job is to reduce coupling to shared machinery

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no module; its sections are measurement intents and its two followups are a localized repair and a session schedule, so there is no interface to judge.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — root-to-relative path resolution is already implemented four times across the tree, and the `minted_from` repair would mint through one of those sites without naming an owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds to none of these families (its followups add a test and a rewrite of committed manifest values, neither of which is one of the four), so no section is required to name a retirement or a merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's one concrete code change (mint `minted_from` repo-relative) names no existing resolver, while `_ledger_relative_path` already performs exactly that root-relative resolution in the same file the change targets.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 moves in the extension direction (reduce this repo's coupling to machinery it does not own — reckon crew/plan, local lane and router, fleet/SLURM placement, imas-python, GPFS paths — to a thin interface over the owner), and no wrapper over repo-owned machinery is proposed.
